title: Attributes
goal: In this lesson you will learn how attributes store data on each object with a dot.
learn: Each object keeps its own values
idea: An attribute is a piece of data stuck on an object. Set it with a dot: dog.name = "Buddy". Read it the same way: print(dog.name). Each object can have different attribute values even if they share a class.
changeOneLine: In the editor above, change dog1.age = 3 to dog1.age = 5. Press Run. First line should say Buddy is 5.

practice.hint: Set pet.kind to a string in quotes (like "cat" or "hamster"). Use print(pet.name) and print(pet.kind).

practice.text: Make two Players with different levels. Print both levels.
practice.hint: Levels are already set on a and b. Print each player's level with print(a.level) and print(b.level).
practice.starterTip: Fill the two print() lines with print(a.level) and print(b.level) — you should see 2 then 7.
practice.starter:
class Player:
    pass
a = Player()
b = Player()
a.level = 2
b.level = 7
print()
print()
practice.gradingNote: Pass if 2 and 7 print from attributes.
